title: Computer vision, image generation and information extraction
learningObjective: Identify features of computer vision and image-generation models, and techniques to extract information from text, images, audio and video.
foundation: Computer vision lets software understand images: describe them, tag them, find objects, and read text in them (OCR).
Image generation models do the opposite: they create new images from a text description, or edit existing ones.

Information extraction pulls specific facts out of content: the total from an invoice, the speaker's main complaint from a call, the scenes in a video. Azure Content Understanding does this for documents, images, audio and video.
engineer: Vision capabilities: captioning (one sentence for the whole image; dense captions for regions), tagging, object detection (bounding boxes with labels), OCR / Read (printed and handwritten text with positions), people detection, smart cropping. Multimodal models add free-form visual question answering and reasoning about charts, screenshots and photos.

Image generation (for example gpt-image-1): text-to-image, image editing with a reference image or mask, size and quality options; prompts and outputs pass content filters; outputs can include content credentials (C2PA provenance). DALL-E 3 has been retired in Foundry; use gpt-image models.

Extraction techniques by modality: text: NER, key phrases, PII, custom extraction with prompts; documents: OCR + layout (tables, selection marks, structure) + fields; images: descriptions, detected objects and text; audio: transcription with diarization, then fields such as summary or sentiment; video: segmentation into scenes, key frames, transcripts and per-segment descriptions.

Azure Content Understanding: analyzers (prebuilt such as prebuilt-invoice, prebuilt-imageSearch, prebuilt-audioSearch, prebuilt-videoSearch, or custom with a field schema). Field methods: Extract (documents only; value as it appears), Classify (pick from categories), Generate (create a value such as a summary). Results include confidence and grounding (where a value came from).
Azure Document Intelligence remains available for classic form and document extraction with prebuilt and custom models.

example.title: An insurer's claims pipeline
body: Customers upload damage photos: a multimodal model describes the damage; OCR reads the licence plate. Content Understanding extracts policy number and date from the claim PDF (Extract), classifies the claim type (Classify) and summarises the recorded phone call (Generate).
Marketing uses gpt-image-1 to create illustrations for claim guides, labelled as AI-generated.

$endpoint = (Get-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai).Endpoint
$key = (Get-AzCognitiveServicesAccountKey -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai).Key1
$r = Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post -Uri "$($endpoint)contentunderstanding/analyzers/prebuilt-invoice:analyze?api-version=2025-11-01" `
  -Headers @{ 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key' = $key } -ContentType 'application/json' -Body '{"inputs":[{"url":"https://contoso.example/invoices/inv-1001.pdf"}]}'
$op = $r.Headers['Operation-Location']
do { Start-Sleep 2; $res = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$op" -Headers @{ 'Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key' = $key } } while ($res.status -notin 'Succeeded','Failed')
$res.result.contents[0].fields
configuration.python:
# pip install requests
import os, time, requests

endpoint = os.environ["CU_ENDPOINT"].rstrip("/")  # https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com
headers = {"Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key": os.environ["CU_KEY"], "Content-Type": "application/json"}
url = f"{endpoint}/contentunderstanding/analyzers/prebuilt-invoice:analyze?api-version=2025-11-01"

resp = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"inputs": [{"url": "https://contoso.example/invoices/inv-1001.pdf"}]})
resp.raise_for_status()  # expect 202 Accepted
operation = resp.headers["Operation-Location"]

while True:
    result = requests.get(operation, headers=headers).json()
    if result["status"] in ("Succeeded", "Failed"):
        break
    time.sleep(2)

for name, field in result["result"]["contents"][0].get("fields", {}).items():
    print(name, field.get("valueString") or field.get("valueNumber") or field.get("valueDate"), field.get("confidence"))

troubleshooting.symptom: OCR misses text in a photo.
Extract field returns nothing for a video.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Generate or Classify for audio and video.

comparisons.difference: Captions describe the image; detection locates objects with boxes.
Content Understanding extracts schema fields across modalities; Language analyses text.

misconceptions.myth: OCR is the same as image captioning.
misconceptions.reality: OCR reads text; captioning describes scenes.
Content filters and provenance credentials apply.

architectureDecisions: Use prebuilt analyzers first, then custom schemas.
Route low-confidence fields to human review.
